column2: Two peasants stand before me, red-faced and shouting, a muddy pig on a rope between them. Each swears by the gods and his grandmother that the beast is his. The steward says the pig has eaten half a field of turnips belonging to a third man, who is shouting too.
I will hear them both out and judge fairly.
Justice is my duty, even for a pig.
The pig is forfeit to my kitchens. Next!

My court priest is in a towering rage. The cook served roast meat on a holy fast day, and when reproached, said in front of the whole hall that the gods do not eat pork, so they will not miss it. Half the court laughed. The priest demands punishment.

My court priest is in a towering rage. The cook served a feast on a day of fasting before the Holy Flame, and when reproached, said in front of the whole hall that Ormazd has more important things to watch than his pots. Half the court laughed. The priest demands punishment.
It was only a joke. Let it pass.
A night in the cells will teach the cook some respect.
The cook will be flogged before the kitchen staff.
Mockery of the gods is death. Hang the cook.
Wolves have come down from the forest and taken half the flocks of the demesne. The bold among my vassals want a great hunt, while the idle ones would rather leave it to the shepherds and their dogs.
Let the shepherds deal with it.
Saddle the horses! We ride with the bold.
I will hunt them down myself, every last one.
My marshal will organise the hunt properly.

A priest at my court has brought a village woman before me in chains. He swears she is a witch: the cows dry up when she passes, and she was seen talking to crows. She looks to me like a frightened midwife, but the villagers are shouting for fire.
She is no witch. Let her go home.
Put her to the ordeal of the river. If she floats, she burns.
Put her to the question. The truth will come out.
So fair a face can only hide a foul soul. Burn her.
Cattle thieves have been caught red-handed with a herd from my demesne. My marshal has them in chains in the courtyard, waiting for my judgement.
They are hungry men. Show them mercy.
Cut off their hands. They will steal no more.
Hang them from the castle walls.
Throw them in the dungeon.
My men have taken a band of brigands who have robbed travellers on the roads for months. They are a ragged lot, deserters and outlaws, and they stand in the courtyard awaiting my word.
Let them go, I have better things to do.
Give them a proper trial before the court.
Off with their heads. Every one.
I will deal with them myself.
Find out who has been feeding them and hiding them.
A rich and unwary lord is staying not far from here with only a few guards. His family would pay handsomely to have him back. I could have him in my dungeon by nightfall.
Seize him!
The lord will be taken and held for ransom.
Masked men burst into my chamber in the dead of night. I have been dragged in chains to the castle of [From.GetTitledName], who now demands a ransom for my release.
I will pay, curse you.
The ransom will be paid.
[From.GetTitledName] has agreed to pay for [From.GetHerHis] freedom. It only remains to decide what terms I will hold [From.GetHerHim] to.
Let [From.GetHerHim] go for a token sum. Easy come, easy go.
A fair ransom, fairly paid, and [From.GetSheHe] goes free.
[From.GetSheHeCap] stays in chains until [From.GetSheHe] pays twice over.
I have changed my mind about the terms.
My spymaster has unmasked a spy in my household, a servant who has been sending letters to one of my rivals for months. The wretch is on his knees before me, begging for his life.
Let him go. He will tell his master that we know.
Behead him.
Lock him away and forget him.
I will beat the names out of him myself.
Put out his eyes. He will spy on no one again.

Shepherds come running down from the hills with tales of a great winged beast that took a whole flock and set the pines alight. Some say it is a dragon woken from its long sleep, others a wyvern from the mountains. My bolder vassals are already sharpening their lances.
Pay a hedge wizard to drive it off.
I will hunt the beast myself!
Bar the gates and stay inside until it is gone.
Let the bold ones have their hunt. Glory to whoever brings back its head.
Poachers have been taking deer from my forest under my very nose. My gamekeepers say there is a whole gang of them, and that the villagers protect them.
The villagers are hungry. Let it be.
My councillors will put an end to it.
One of your councillors will hunt down the poachers.
My liege has asked me to deal with the poachers in the forest. After a week of watching the trails, my men have caught them with a deer on a pole between them: three thin villagers and a boy.
Let them go with a warning.
Take them to my liege for judgement.
The poachers will be brought before your liege.
My [From.GetTitle] [From.GetFirstName] has brought the poachers before me: three thin villagers and a boy, with a deer between them.
A fine will do. Let them go.
Hang them, but with a silken rope, as the law allows.
Release them. What is a deer or two?
Kill them where they stand.
Cut off their ears, so all will know them for thieves.
Your councillor will see the sentence carried out.
My liege has passed sentence on the poachers, and I am to see it carried out.
A hanging is the law. It is fitting.
Hanging hungry men for a deer is cruel.
Their ears are a fair price for their crime.
Maiming a boy for a deer is cruel.
They knew the price of poaching.
Butchering villagers for a deer is cruel.
Your councillor approves of the sentence.
My [From.GetTitle] [From.GetFirstName] has carried out the sentence and tells me that the villagers think it a just one.
Good.
Your councillor thinks the sentence cruel.
My [From.GetTitle] [From.GetFirstName] has carried out the sentence, but made no secret of thinking it cruel. The villagers mutter about it in the taverns.
Let them mutter.

I have been robbed! A cutpurse in the market took my purse, and my lodgings were broken into while I slept. The lands of [Root.Host.GetTitledName] are crawling with thieves and robbers. I must complain.
I will complain to my host.
Your host will hear your complaint.
[From.GetTitledName] complains that [From.GetSheHe] was robbed in my lands. My men have even caught one of the thieves, a ragged young man who begs for mercy.
You should have kept a closer eye on your purse.
The thief goes to the dungeon.
Hang the thief.
Cut off his hands.
The thief will be punished.
[From.GetTitledName] has passed sentence on the thief who robbed me.
He deserved the rope.
A hanging for a purse? That is too much.
He will steal no more.
A boy's hands for a purse? That is cruel.
The dungeon is where he belongs.
Throwing a starving boy in the dungeon is no justice.
[From.GetTitledName] approves of the sentence.
[From.GetTitledName] thanks me for seeing justice done.
It was my duty.
[From.GetTitledName] thinks the sentence cruel.
[From.GetTitledName] says that the sentence was cruel, and that [From.GetSheHe] wishes [From.GetSheHe] had never complained.
There is no pleasing some people.

My [Root.Spouse.GetHusbandWife] has been unfaithful again, and makes no secret of it. The whole court laughs behind my back. My host, [Root.Host.GetTitledName], is the only one who can put a stop to it.
I will ask my host for justice.
I will bear it in silence and pray.
Your host will hear your complaint.

[From.GetTitledName] has come to me in tears. [From.GetHerHis] [From.Spouse.GetHusbandWife] [From.Spouse.GetFirstName] has been unfaithful, and the whole court knows it. [From.GetSheHeCap] asks me to punish [From.Spouse.GetHerHim].
What happens in their bedchamber is no business of mine.
Throw the faithless one in the dungeon!
Faithlessness is no crime. Pleasure is its own reward.
A day in the stocks will cool that hot blood.
The faithless spouse goes unpunished.
[From.GetTitledName] will do nothing about my faithless [Root.Spouse.GetHusbandWife].
I am a laughing-stock.
The faithless spouse will be punished.
[From.GetTitledName] has punished my faithless [Root.Spouse.GetHusbandWife]. Let the court laugh now.
Justice is done.
The faithless spouse will resent you for it.
[From.GetTitledName] has punished me for my little pleasures, and all because my [Root.Spouse.GetHusbandWife] went whining to [From.GetHerHim]. I will not forget it.
How humiliating.
The day is clear and the wind is right, and my vassals and I have ridden out with our hawks. My falcon has just taken a heron in full view of the whole party.
Did you see that? The finest bird in the realm!
Praise the boldest riders.
Hardly notice the others at all.

I am holding a banquet for the court. My old friend [invitation_pending.GetTitledName] would be glad of an invitation, though [invitation_pending.GetSheHe] does tend to drink too much and pick fights.
Of course [invitation_pending.GetSheHe] must come.
Not this time.
Your friend will be invited to the banquet.
Your friend may hear about the banquet and be hurt.
My friend [From.GetTitledName] has invited me to a banquet.
I am afraid I cannot come.
I will be there.
I would not miss it for the world!
My friend [From.GetTitledName] held a banquet, and I was not invited. I had to hear about it from a servant.
I am sure there was a reason. I will forgive [From.GetHerHim].
I will sulk.
I will tell [From.GetHerHim] what I think of it.
Your friend will tell you what [From.GetSheHe] thinks.
My friend [From.GetTitledName] has come to ask why [From.GetSheHe] was not invited to my banquet, and is clearly hurt.
So? It was my banquet.
I am sorry. It will not happen again.
The banquet is over, and the hall is a ruin of bones, spilled wine and snoring guests.
A pity [From.GetFirstName] could not come.
It was good to see [From.GetFirstName] again.
[From.GetFirstName] was the soul of the party!
It is market day, and the square is full of merchants, peddlers, livestock and pickpockets. My vassals have come along to see what can be had.
Buy everything that catches my eye!
Haggle every merchant down to the bone.
Bargain hard and loud. Let them call me a miser.
Share a drink with the merchants.
Show my vassals how a lord should be seen in the market.
The knights of my court hold a joust in honour of the Lady. The lists are hung with banners, the ladies have given their favours, and the finest lance at my court waits for my signal.
Let the jousting begin!
Grown men knocking each other off horses. How droll.
Praise the champion before the whole court.
I will ride in the lists myself!
Spend the whole joust holding court in my pavilion.
Give the prizes to the poor knights.
A great tourney is held in my lands, and knights have come from across Bretonnia to break lances for the Lady's glory. My bravest vassals look to me to ride in it.
I will watch from the stands, thank you.
Spare no expense, and I will ride myself!
Which end of the lance do I hold?
Bless the knights before they ride.
Cheer on my vassals.
The village is holding its harvest festival, with dancing, drinking and a greasy pole. My vassals are there, and so, unfortunately, is one of my rivals.
Spend the evening with my vassals.
Watch the peasants make fools of themselves.
Join the dancing!
Pay for drinks for the whole village.
One of my old vassals has wed a girl a third his age, and the whole court is at the wedding feast. The bride looks miserable, the groom looks very pleased with himself, and the wine is good.
Raise a toast to the happy couple!
Make a joke about the wedding night.
Eat and drink everything in sight.
A wandering bard is singing in the hall, and his song is about me. It is not flattering. My vassals are trying very hard not to laugh.
Ignore him.
Have him beaten and thrown out!
Leave the hall without a word.
Laugh along, and reward him for his wit.
Answer him with a better verse of my own.
Your vassal will see what you do.
The bard sang a mocking song about my liege, and I watched how [From.GetTitledName] took it.
Beating a bard for a song is petty.
To laugh at oneself is the mark of a great lord.
Your vassal thinks you cruel.
My vassal [From.GetTitledName] makes no secret that beating the bard was petty and cruel.
Perhaps I was too harsh.
Your vassal admires your good humour.
My vassal [From.GetTitledName] praises my good humour before the whole court. The bard has written a new song, this one rather flattering.
A lord must be able to laugh.

An old man in rags has come to my gates, claiming to be my late father. He says he was led astray in the forest of Athel Loren and kept for one night in the hall of the Wood Elves' queen, and that a night there is many years here. He sings songs no one has ever heard, and he knows things about our family that only my father could know.
Whoever he is, give him food and a warm bed.
A spy of my enemies, no doubt.
Throw the madman out!
Watch him closely. There is something wrong here.
Welcome home, father!
Listen to his songs all night.

A troubadour and his wife the trobairitz have arrived from Tilea. Their performances range from vulgar satires to political sirventes and everything in between, including songs and poems of courtly love.
Courtly love. How tedious.
Enough! Sing something with a battle in it.
Listen closely to the verses.
Listen closely to who the satires are about.
Seat them with my most learned vassal.
Pay them well, and send them on their way with gifts.

To amuse the court, a few of us dressed as wild men of the forest, sewn into costumes of linen, pitch and flax. Someone came too close with a torch. In an instant the hall is full of screaming, burning men.
Fire! FIRE!
Throw myself into a vat of wine!
Roll on the floor and pray!
